messages.subject: problem with increment_log_prob() and nan:0
parts:
Dear Stan users,

I'm new to Stan and have some trouble in change of variables.

Here is my first code with increment_log_prob() : 

data {
    int<lower=0> J;          // number of subjects
    real BP[J];             
    real logBP[J];
    real logVarSE[J];  // log(sigma_epsilon square)
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> mu;
  real<lower=0> sigmabeta;
  real<lower=0> tau1;
  real<lower=0> tau2;
  real<lower=0> theta[J];
  real<lower=0> sigmaepsilon[J];
  real beta0;
  real beta1;
}

transformed parameters{
        real<lower=0> logVar[J];
        logVar[J]<- log(sigmaepsilon[J]^2);
}

model {       

    for (j in 1:J) {

    BP[j] ~ normal(theta[j],sigmaepsilon[j]);
    theta[j] ~ normal(mu,sigmabeta);

    logVar[j] ~ normal(beta0 + beta1*logBP[j],tau1);
    increment_log_prob(log(2)-log(sigmaepsilon[j]));

    logVarSE[j] ~ normal(logVar[j], tau2);   
    }
    
I transformed sigmaepsilon[j] to log(sigmaepsilon[J]^2) and wrote “increment_log_prob(log(2)-log(sigmaepsilon[j]))” in my model (derivative of the transform log(sigmaepsilon[J]^2) = 2/sigmaepsilon[J], and log(| 2/sigmaepsilon[J] |) = log(2)-log(sigmaepsilon[J])  ). I'm confused why stan still gives the warning that I did not do transformation: 

Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
 You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.

Then I wrote my second code and tried  "increment_log_prob(normal_log(log(2)-logVar[j], beta0 + beta1*logBP[j], tau1))". 
Stan did not give me the warning this time, but I received the following error: 

Invalid value of logVar: validate transformed params(N4stan5agrad3varE): logVar[k0__] is nan:0, but must be greater than or equal to 0

I don't know why I'm getting this error, I thought I specified that "real<lower=0> sigmaepsilon[J]" and "real<lower=0> logVar[J]" in the parameter block. I must be missing something about the syntax in Stan. 

How should I do the change of variable and fix the error? Any help is much appreciated! 

-- Chubing Zeng

    real logVarSE[J];  // log(sigma_epsilon square)

  real<lower=0> sigmaepsilon[J];

}

    for (j in 1:J) {
    BP[j] ~ normal(theta[j],sigmaepsilon[j]);
    theta[j] ~ normal(mu,sigmabeta);
    increment_log_prob(normal_log(log(2)-logVar[j], beta0 + beta1*logBP[j], tau1));
    logVarSE[j] ~ normal(logVar[j], tau2);   

    }

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: problem with increment_log_prob() and nan:0
parts:
Hi,

The problem is that you've defined logVar[J] (note: "J", capital J, it's a number, say... 10), but you haven't defined logVar[1], logVar[2], ..., logVar[J - 1]. Those values are set to NaN (not a number).

The fix is to use a loop for logVar (inside transformed parameters):
for (j in 1:J)

logVar[j] <- log(square(sigmaepsilon[J]))

(there may be other problems with your model, but see if that gets you past the error.)




Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: problem with increment_log_prob() and nan:0
parts: You're right that the error about the location parameter for normal_log is non-fatal. When is it happening? If it's only occurring a few times during warmup then you can ignore it. If it's happening a lot and during sampling (post-warmup) then it's a concern.
